item.title: Russian troops seize settlement of Tersyanka in southeast Ukraine
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-15
MOSCOW -- Russian forces have captured the settlement of Tersyanka in southeastern Ukraine's Zaporozhye region and taken control of a Ukrainian fortified area spanning more than 10 square kilometers, the Russian Defense Ministry said Saturday. Assault units seized the settlement and cleared more than 300 buildings, the ministry said, according to TASS news agency. The Ukrainian armed forces lost more than 1,000 troops in the special military operation zone over the past 24 hours as a result of operations by Russian battle groups, the report said.

item.title: SpaceX catches Starship for first time
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-15
LOS ANGELES -- SpaceX's Starship spacecraft returned to its launch site on Saturday and was caught by the launch tower's mechanical arms, completing Starship's 15th flight test. It marked the first time a Starship spacecraft had been caught by the launch tower's mechanical arms upon returning to the launch site. The giant rocket lifted off from SpaceX's Starbase facility in the US state of Texas on Friday afternoon. After about 22 and a half hours, the spacecraft returned to the launch site at about 3:20 pm Central Time. The mission was designed to attempt the first-ever catch of both the Super Heavy booster and the Starship spacecraft by the launch tower's mechanical arms during a single flight. However, after stage separation, the booster was diverted from its planned return to the launch site and made an offshore splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico. The Starship spacecraft performed its orbital insertion burn and entered Earth's orbit. It later deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites. Following payload deploy, Starship entered a prolonged coast phase in orbit. After more than 20 hours in space, the SpaceX flight control team began preparations for the spacecraft's return to the launch site. Starship successfully reignited one of its Raptor sea-level engines and performed a deorbit burn, leaving orbit and beginning its descent toward Earth. The spacecraft then made its way back toward the Texas coast, executing a final swoop maneuver over the Gulf of Mexico before approaching the launch site from which it had lifted off. After emerging from the clouds, Starship ignited three Raptor engines to perform its landing flip maneuver and slow its descent toward the launch tower. The tower's mechanical arms then successfully caught the spacecraft, marking the first such catch of a Starship vehicle. In its previous flight test on Sept 28, Starship reached orbit for the first time and deployed 26 next-generation Starlink V3 satellites. SpaceX's Starship spacecraft and Super Heavy rocket, collectively referred to as Starship, represent a fully reusable transportation system designed to carry both crew and cargo to Earth orbit, the Moon, Mars and beyond.

item.title: China men's football team ends losing streak
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-15
ZHAOQING, China -- China ended a losing streak with a 2-0 home victory over Malaysia in an international friendly here on Saturday, with Wang Yudong and Zhang Yuning scoring in the first half. China had lost three consecutive friendlies in last international window, suffering a 3-0 defeat to New Zealand in September before falling 5-0 to Palestine and 1-0 to Tajikistan in October. With most of its key players back in the squad, China made a positive start and took the lead in the 10th minute. Following a series of passes down the right flank, Lin Liangming delivered a cross into the penalty area, where 20-year-old forward Wang arrived at the far post to head home. China doubled its lead nine minutes later, when Wang Shangyuan sent a well-weighted ball over the Malaysian defense from midfield, and Zhang chipped the ball over the goalkeeper from inside the penalty area. Tensions flared between the two sides in first-half stoppage time. After reviewing the incident on VAR, the referee showed yellow cards to China assistant coach Zhou Ting and Malaysia defender Tan Jun Jin. China enjoyed 59 percent possession in the first half and registered six shots, two on target, while Malaysia managed three attempts without a shot on target. The Chinese head coach Shao Jiayi made seven substitutions during the second half, and the host's attacking threat diminished. Malaysia thought it had pulled a goal back in the 77th minute when Fergus Tierney capitalized on a defensive error by China. However, after another VAR review, the referee ruled out the goal for a foul in the build-up. China goalkeeper Li Hao made two crucial saves in the closing stages to preserve the clean sheet. In the 90th minute, Tierney was sent off after receiving a second yellow card for a foul, as China held on to secure a 2-0 victory. "The match was not easy. As a coach, whether looking at the process or the result, I am very satisfied with what the players showed. The league season has just ended and everyone is very tired. For them to generate such enthusiasm, passion and team spirit at this point in time is exactly what the Chinese team needs," Shao said at the post match news conference. The 46-year-old urged that the players still need to stay calm. "This victory is very important, but we have no reason to be overly optimistic. The opponents had nearly 20 players unavailable, yet they still possess certain strength -- this is the current reality of Asian football. We cannot take any team or any match lightly." The Chinese side will play against Bahrain next Tuesday. "We have only two days to recover before the next match, which is very difficult, but professional players must get used to and adapt to this kind of situation. I believe they can perform better in the next match," he added.

item.title: Preparations for APEC Shenzhen meeting ready: officials
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-14
SHENZHEN -- Preparations for the 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, South China, are ready, local officials said at a press briefing on Saturday. The 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting will be held in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, on Nov 18 and 19, Wang Xi, deputy head of the provincial preparatory leading group, told the briefing. Wang said organizers had incorporated green practices, traditional Chinese and local Lingnan culture, and digital technologies into venue preparations and services. During the meeting week, Guangdong will offer 218 visitor sites and 43 routes, including two representative ones in Shenzhen. Organizers have upgraded key venues and conducted comprehensive rehearsals, and have arranged reception, accommodation, catering, transport, medical care and interpretation, as well as measures for communications, weather, public security, public health and city operations, Wang said. Shenzhen Mayor Li Yun said all venues and facilities were ready. The city has strengthened transport, power, communications and hotel services while minimizing inconvenience to residents' daily lives. The city has also introduced measures to make travel and daily transactions easier for visiting delegates. Dedicated channels for meeting representatives will be available at nine sea, land, air and rail ports. More than 100,000 foreign-language signs have been standardized, and over 7,000 AI translation devices have been installed at key locations. Taxis will provide bilingual announcements. More than 3,000 ATMs support cash withdrawal for foreign bank cards, while over 1,600 bank branches offer currency exchange. Shenzhen's metro fare gates will accept contactless payments with overseas bank cards. The city has also expanded its departure tax-refund program to 3,160 stores, including more than 1,000 offering instant refunds. Data released at the briefing also showed that Shenzhen has become the first city in the Chinese mainland to record more than 5 trillion yuan ($744.6 billion) in foreign trade. Shenzhen Customs said the city's imports and exports totaled 5.25 trillion yuan in the first 10 months of this year, up 40.9 percent year-on-year. Exports rose 19.7 percent to 2.71 trillion yuan, while imports surged 73.7 percent to 2.54 trillion yuan.

item.title: Museum expo aims to strengthen intl exchanges
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-14
The 11th Chinese Exposition of Museums and Relevant Products and Technologies opened on Friday in the coastal city of Haikou, capital of Hainan province, with Egypt serving as the expo's first-ever country of honor — a move that experts said signals a broader push to strengthen international museum exchanges. As the largest and most influential expo in China's museum sector, the event has been held biennially since 2004. This year, it brings together almost 600 museums and around 200 cultural heritage-related enterprises in Haikou, showcasing cutting-edge advances in the protection of cultural relics, digital museums, exhibition display technology and cultural creative products. The theme this year is "Museums for High-Quality Development: Empowering with Technology, Connecting with the Future". The four-day event features 12 thematic areas, including achievements in museum development, digital and intelligent technologies, international exhibitors, non-State-owned museums and cultural heritage corporations. The expo introduced a country-of-honor mechanism, with Egypt serving in this capacity. Three major Egyptian cultural institutions — the Grand Egyptian Museum, the Egyptian Museum in Cairo and the National Museum of Egyptian Civilization — are taking part in the international exhibitors' area. French institutions, including Universcience — Cite des Sciences et de l'Industrie in Paris, are also exhibiting. Guan Qiang, president of the Chinese Museums Association, said that while the expo had previously hosted foreign museums, no participating nation had been given the status of a country of honor. By introducing this format, the organizers hope to strengthen future exchanges with the museum sectors of other countries.

item.title: Asia-Pacific needs digital bridges, not 'digital fences'
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
During an interview with China Daily's Global Lens, Ong Tee Keat, president of the Belt and Road Initiative Caucus for Asia Pacific in Malaysia, stresses inclusive digital supply chain finance, local-currency settlement and inclusive credit — rejecting "small yards and high fences"— plus capacity building so the digital dividend leaves no one behind. During the interview, Ong says China-ASEAN Free Trade Area 3.0 putting digital trade and sustainable innovation at the core of regional integration. More supportive measures will release a great regional market potential. Ong adds that interoperable digital frameworks let small traders access regional value chains through QR payments, e-commerce and paperless customs. But compliance burdens and tech disruption can marginalize grassroots entrepreneurs and uneven digital readiness makes coordination hard. Therefore, the region needs more coordinative efforts to solve the problems. (Reporter: Li Wei, Video: Pan Yixuan)
